raw.description:
Become a part of our caring community

Services represent one of the organization’s most consequential sources of capability, capacity, transformation and external spend. The Associate Vice President, Services Procurement will lead the enterprise strategy for contingent workforce, outsourcing and offshoring, consulting and clinical services, converting third-party services into measurable business outcomes, workforce agility, operating leverage and sustainable value.
The AVP will serve as the senior Procurement partner to leaders across the Insurance segment and Corporate Services, helping shape operating-model, workforce and transformation decisions before sourcing begins or a supplier solution is selected.
The leader will bring deep expertise in global business services, business process outsourcing, workforce solutions and complex professional services. The mandate is to strengthen business-case quality, establish clear make, buy, build, automate and partner choices, create fit-for-purpose commercial models, manage transitions and hold providers accountable for committed outcomes.
Success will be measured by whether business leaders make better services and workforce decisions, transformations deliver their promised value, and suppliers improve performance and innovation.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the Strategic Services Partner to Business Leaders

  • Serve as the senior Procurement relationship leader and trusted commercial advisor to Insurance segment and Corporate Services leadership.
  • Develop a deep understanding of business strategy, operating plans, transformation roadmaps, workforce needs and financial commitments, and translate them into integrated services, workforce and supplier strategies.
  • Engage upstream of supplier selection to frame the problem, test demand and assess make, buy, build, automate, offshore, outsource and partner alternatives.
  • Bring concise, decision-ready recommendations that clarify business outcomes, value, cost, risk, capacity, speed, optionality and organizational implications.
  • Create alignment across business, Finance, HR, Legal, Risk, Compliance, Technology and Procurement before material commitments are made.
  • Build credibility and operating mechanisms for Procurement to function as an extension of business leadership rather than a downstream execution team.

Lead Enterprise Workforce, Outsourcing and Services Strategy

  • Own enterprise category strategies for contingent workforce, outsourcing and offshoring, consulting and clinical services, with clear boundaries and coordination across adjacent functions.
  • Build an integrated external workforce strategy spanning employee alternatives, temporary labor, statement-of-work services, managed services, outsourcing and offshore delivery.
  • Design location and delivery-model strategies that consider capability, labor economics, automation potential, regulatory and contractual constraints, data access, resiliency, concentration, talent supply and change impact.
  • Advance global business services models by helping leaders evaluate retained organization design, service placement, process ownership, governance, centers of excellence and provider ecosystems.
  • Establish multi-year category strategies grounded in demand forecasts, business roadmaps, market intelligence, benchmarks, supplier economics and emerging service models.
  • Maintain a forward-looking pipeline of transformation, sourcing, demand-management, insource/outsource, supplier optimization and commercial-model opportunities.

Raise the Standard for Business Cases and Transformation Decisions

  • Create a rigorous, enterprise approach to business cases for outsourcing, offshoring, consulting and workforce transformation.
  • Ensure cases are grounded in validated baselines, fully loaded current-state cost, demand and volume assumptions, productivity, implementation and transition costs, technology dependencies, stranded costs, retained-organization requirements, risk and timing.
  • Pressure-test whether proposed value comes from sustainable process improvement, automation and operating-model redesign rather than labor arbitrage alone.
  • Partner with Finance to validate assumptions, establish credible baselines and track in-year, run-rate and realized value after implementation.
  • Define decision gates and executive accountabilities from strategy through sourcing, transition, stabilization and benefit realization.
  • Challenge proposals that lack clear outcomes, executable change plans, realistic capacity assumptions or sufficient protections against value leakage.

Drive Commercial Strategy and Complex Negotiations

  • Personally lead or sponsor the organization’s most complex, highest-value and highest-risk services negotiations.
  • Build negotiation strategies using benchmarks, supplier economics, competitive alternatives, incumbent leverage, switching costs, demand aggregation and enterprise-wide relationships.
  • Design commercial models suited to the work, including rate-card, milestone, transaction, consumption, capacity, managed-service, outcome-based, gainshare and hybrid constructs.
  • Strengthen contractual protections for pricing, productivity, benchmarking, service levels, innovation, continuous improvement, change control, audit, transition, termination and exit assistance.
  • Distinguish true strategic consulting from staff augmentation and managed services, ensuring that scope, talent, rates and accountability match the work being purchased.
  • Partner with Finance to ensure negotiated value is credible, visible and translated into measurable enterprise impact.

Build a High-Performing Contingent Workforce Model

  • Define the enterprise contingent workforce strategy, governance and supplier architecture across temporary labor, independent talent, direct sourcing, statement-of-work services and managed solutions.
  • Improve demand planning, talent-channel selection, rate and markup governance, supplier performance, tenure management, worker quality and speed to productivity.
  • Create transparency across external labor demand, skills, location, cost, supplier concentration and conversion opportunities.
  • Partner with HR, business leaders, Finance, Legal and Risk to clarify ownership, controls and decision rights across the external workforce lifecycle.
  • Use market intelligence, workforce analytics, direct sourcing, talent pools, automation and modern workforce platforms to improve quality, access, agility and cost.
  • Prevent misclassification and channel leakage by establishing clear distinctions among contingent labor, consulting, outsourcing and employee roles.

Shape Strategic Consulting and Clinical Services

  • Establish enterprise consulting strategies, preferred-partner models and governance that match supplier capability and commercial model to the nature of the work.
  • Improve visibility to consulting demand, reduce fragmented buying, challenge unnecessary work and ensure knowledge transfer and measurable deliverables.
  • Build fit-for-purpose category and supplier strategies for clinical services, balancing quality, access, member and patient outcomes, cost, compliance, delegation and operational continuity.
  • Partner with clinical, legal, compliance, network and risk leaders to clarify which services Procurement leads, co-leads or routes through specialized contracting channels.
  • Apply differentiated sourcing and governance based on whether services involve direct care, licensed professionals, delegated activity, claims reimbursement, sensitive data or value-based arrangements.
  • Ensure service quality and continuity are treated as primary outcomes, not trade-offs against financial value.

Build a Modern, Commercially Formidable Team

  • Lead, coach and develop Category Managers, Supplier Managers and procurement professionals with clear expectations for business partnership, commercial judgment, analytical rigor and measurable impact.
  • Build deep capabilities in global business services, outsourcing, workforce economics, consulting, clinical services, business-case development, transition management, complex negotiation and executive influence.
  • Shift the team from processing requests to shaping operating-model and workforce decisions, anticipating opportunities and challenging assumptions constructively.
  • Increase strategic capacity by simplifying work, using shared services and embedding analytics, automation and AI into market intelligence, business cases, negotiations, contracts and supplier monitoring.
  • Establish clear performance standards, succession plans and development opportunities that strengthen the broader Procurement leadership bench.
  • Create an environment where leaders operate independently with senior executives, make difficult decisions and remain accountable for outcomes.

How Success Will Be Measured

  • Delivery of validated financial, workforce, transformation and broader enterprise-value commitments.
  • Finance-aligned business cases with validated baselines, transparent assumptions and clear benefit-realization ownership.
  • Multi-year strategies covering the substantial majority of addressable services spend and external workforce demand.
  • Improved visibility to contingent labor, consulting, outsourcing and clinical-services demand, commitments, suppliers and risks.
  • Measurable improvement in cycle time, stakeholder experience and quality of commercial decisions.
  • Greater adoption of fit-for-purpose workforce channels, preferred providers and standardized commercial models.
  • Outsourcing and offshoring programs meeting transition, service, financial, transformation and risk commitments.
  • Reduced fragmented buying, rate leakage, unmanaged statements of work, supplier proliferation and surprise renewals.
  • Improvement in supplier quality, service, productivity, innovation, resiliency and contractual value realization.
  • Increased confidence from Insurance and Corporate Services leadership.
  • Stronger talent, succession readiness and organizational capability.


Use your skills to make an impact

Required Qualifications

  • 15+ years of progressive experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Global Business Services, Business Process Outsourcing, Workforce Solutions, Consulting, Supplier Management or related commercial leadership roles.
  • 10+ years of people leadership experience, including success building, transforming and retaining high-performing teams.
  • Deep expertise in several relevant domains, including contingent workforce, outsourcing and offshoring, consulting, managed services, business process services or clinical services.
  • Demonstrated experience designing or sourcing global business services models, including retained-organization design, service placement, transition and provider governance.
  • Exceptional business-case acuity, including baseline validation, fully loaded cost analysis, productivity, implementation, transition, stranded cost, retained cost, risk and benefit realization.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex services portfolios, executive-level transformations and high-value strategic negotiations.
  • Expertise in services commercial models, supplier economics, labor markets, rate structures, service levels, benchmarking, productivity and outcome-based constructs.
  • Proven ability to advise segment presidents, functional executives and other senior leaders and influence decisions without relying on positional authority.
  • Track record of delivering material enterprise value while protecting service quality, workforce experience, customer or member outcomes, compliance, resiliency and risk.
  • Experience navigating complex transitions, change management, supplier remediation and exit strategies.
  • Experience operating across highly matrixed business, Finance, HR, Legal, Risk, Compliance, Technology and Procurement organizations.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a Fortune 500, healthcare, insurance, highly regulated or similarly complex enterprise.
  • Experience with clinical or healthcare services, delegated arrangements, regulated operations or customer-facing service delivery.
  • Experience leading large-scale outsourcing, offshoring, shared-services or global business services transformations.

TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, empowers organizations with full AI visibility and consolidated security that inspires confidence, drives innovation, and eliminates risk.

At TrendAI™, we’re always seeking exceptional talent; people who want to collaborate with the best and push boundaries together. Here, your work goes beyond building a career. You will help protect what matters and play a vital role in shaping a safer, more trustworthy AI-powered future.

AI Fearlessly.

POSITION OVERVIEW

As a Customer Success Technical Advisor (CSTA), you are the strategic technical linchpin for TrendAI's enterprise clients. Your mission is to move beyond reactive troubleshooting to become a Trusted Advisor, ensuring customers achieve measurable cybersecurity resilience. You will lead the technical journey for our most strategic accounts, transforming complex security requirements into scalable, operational successes within the TrendAI Vision One™ ecosystem.


PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Strategic Technical Advocacy

  • Outcome-Driven Management: Act as the primary technical voice post-deployment, shifting the focus from "ticket resolution" to "security outcome attainment."
  • Success Planning: Contribute technical milestones to the broader Customer Success Plan, ensuring a clear roadmap for platform adoption, version upgrades, and feature deployments.
  • Platform Mastery: Conduct regular architectural reviews and configuration audits to ensure customers are utilizing the full breadth of the TrendAI platform.

2. Proactive Operations & Enablement

  • Value Realization: Guide clients through a structured onboarding and deployment process, ensuring rapid time-to-value and high feature utilization.
  • Technical Workshops: Design and deliver bespoke workshops and "Best Practice" sessions to mature the customer's internal SOC and SIEM operations.
  • Advanced Threat Defense: Provide technical oversight during critical security events, offering proactive recommendations to harden the customer's posture against evolving threats.

3. Operational Excellence & Leadership

  • Root Cause Strategy: Perform deep-dive root cause analysis (RCA) on complex issues, providing long-term strategic recommendations to prevent systemic failures.
  • Cross-Functional Orchestration: Serve as the regional liaison between the customer and internal Product Engineering, R&D, and Sales Engineering to influence product roadmaps.
  • Account Health Integrity: Maintain a "Single Source of Truth" for account health, including detailed environment maps, troubleshooting playbooks, and operational reports.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

  • Language: Fluent in written & spoken English & Spanish, Portuguese is an advantage
  • Experience: 10 or more years of experience in technical support, security architecture, systems engineering, or a relevant client-facing consulting field.
  • Domain Expertise: Strong knowledge of security frameworks (NIST, MITRE ATT&CK), SIEM/SOC operations, and endpoint/network defense technologies.
  • Technical Depth: Deep understanding of multiple operating systems (Windows Server, Linux, Solaris) and hybrid-cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP).
  • Strategic Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to articulate complex technical risks in simple, business-centric terms for executive stakeholders.
  • Analytical Mindset: Highly process-oriented with a passion for digital organization, documentation, and technical reporting.
  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent is preferred.
  • Certifications: Technical certifications are strongly preferred (e.g., TCAP, TSCE, CISSP, CCNA, CCNP, or Cloud Platform Certifications).

At Trend Micro, we embrace change, empower people, and encourage innovation in a connected world. Our diversity and multicultural workforce are key contributing factors to our success across the globe. We like to have fun while taking our culture seriously. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to this regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, nationality, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, gender identity or veteran status. Join us at Varicent—where your talent and ambition meet limitless opportunities for success!

As a QA Analyst, you will be supporting the quality, reliability and performance of Varicent's Incentives application, designed to automate, model and manage complex sales compensation plans. The role is responsible for identifying issues, contributing to process improvements, and helping ensure a seamless user experience. Working under the guidance of senior staff, you will be testing low to moderate complexity issues, developing testing requirements from that direction. Work performed in this role directly supports the trust users place in the platform.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performs manual testing to validate new features and bug fixes.
  • Validates API responses and tests database interactions to ensure system reliability.
  • Identifies and reports defects, providing clear and detailed information, for small-size projects, working under the guidance of senior staff.
  • Identifies, documents, and prioritizes bugs in JIRA or similar tools.
  • Re-tests fixed defects and performs regression testing before releases.
  • Works on simple defects unaided and contributes to testing medium-size projects with guidance.
  • Identifies "happy path" and negative tests based on given requirements.
  • Identifies the scope of small features or fixes based on overall business goals.
  • Identifies the priority of test cases and provides estimates for assignments.
  • Works with QA and development peers to analyze technical problems and escalates problems to leads.
  • Contributes to refining the QA process by identifying inefficiencies and suggesting improvements.
  • Stays current on QA trends and tools to improve testing practices.
  • Takes action to improve processes and makes sound, timely decisions using the information and resources available.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

  • • 0–2 years of experience.
  • • Basic knowledge of software testing methodologies, including manual testing.
  • • Familiarity with QA tools such as JIRA or Postman.
  • • Basic understanding of REST APIs and database testing.
  • • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.
  • • Good understanding of product functionality and architecture and how it fits into the business.
  • • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • • Ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams.
  • • B2 level English or higher is required.

FIRST 30 DAYS: GETTING STARTED

  • Familiarize yourself with the product, team structure, and development workflow.
  • Understand the testing framework and review existing test cases and reports.
  • Start testing minor features and logging bugs to learn the system.
  • Participate in team meetings and shadow senior QA analysts during test planning sessions.

FIRST 60 DAYS: BUILDING MOMENTUM

  • Take ownership of writing and executing test cases for client bugs, small features or modules.
  • Collaborate with the development team to test more complex features and identify potential edge cases.

FIRST 90 DAYS: HITTING YOUR STRIDE

  • Gained increased knowledge of the System under test
  • Increased ownership of testing tasks or projects
  • Provide feedback to the team on onboarding processes and identify areas for improvement in QA workflows.

raw.description:
About Matter Health

Matter Health delivers primary and preventive healthcare directly to Medicare-eligible individuals living in affordable housing communities.

Our mission is simple: improve healthcare access by meeting patients where they are. Through relationship-based, value-driven care, we help individuals live healthier, more independent lives while reducing barriers to high-quality healthcare.

As we continue expanding across the country, we are looking for physician leaders who are passionate about advancing value-based care and developing high-performing clinical teams dedicated to improving the health of the communities we serve.

Total Healthcare. Where you live.

About the Role

Matter Health is seeking an experienced, mission-driven Market Medical Director to provide physician leadership for our Massachusetts market while supporting relationship-based, value-driven care for Medicare-eligible individuals living in affordable housing communities.

This is a fully remote physician leadership position with limited, occasional travel within the assigned market for team engagement, community visits, clinical observation, or other business needs. Routine daily travel and regularly scheduled in-home patient visits are not expected.

The Market Medical Director will provide clinical leadership, physician oversight, provider mentorship, and strategic support to Nurse Practitioners and interdisciplinary care teams. This role also supports population health, quality improvement, care coordination, and the continued development of Matter Health’s community-based care model.

You will partner closely with Nurse Practitioners, Registered Nurses, Patient Advocate/Liaisons, Operations leaders, and other clinical stakeholders to ensure patients receive high-quality, coordinated care.

This position is ideal for a physician who enjoys developing providers, improving clinical outcomes, supporting value-based care initiatives, and helping shape an innovative healthcare delivery model for individuals who may face significant barriers to accessing care.

Work Arrangement

  • Fully remote position supporting the Massachusetts market

  • Limited, occasional travel within the assigned market

  • Virtual collaboration with clinical, operational, and organizational leaders

  • Travel may include team meetings, community engagement, clinical observation, or other business-related needs

  • Routine field travel and regularly scheduled in-home patient visits are not expected

Responsibilities

  • Provide physician leadership and clinical oversight across the Massachusetts market

  • Mentor and support Nurse Practitioners and interdisciplinary care teams

  • Provide clinical consultation and support through virtual collaboration

  • Support clinical decision-making and transitions of care for high-risk patients

  • Drive quality-improvement initiatives and value-based care outcomes

  • Partner with Operations leadership to improve patient experience and market performance

  • Support provider development through coaching, education, and clinical leadership

  • Collaborate with specialists, hospitals, health plans, and community organizations to strengthen care coordination

  • Help develop clinical workflows, best practices, and care-delivery strategies

  • Monitor clinical quality, patient outcomes, and opportunities for continuous improvement

  • Support population-health initiatives across the assigned market

  • Serve as a physician ambassador for Matter Health and the communities we serve

  • Travel within the assigned market occasionally for team, clinical, community, or business needs

Qualifications

  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO)

  • Board Certified or Board Eligible in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, or another applicable primary care specialty

  • Active, unrestricted Massachusetts medical license or the ability to obtain Massachusetts licensure

  • Minimum of five years of physician experience, preferably in primary care

  • Experience leading, mentoring, or providing oversight to clinical teams

  • Strong communication, leadership, and relationship-building skills

  • Ability to lead effectively and collaborate across clinical and operational teams in a remote environment

  • Commitment to serving Medicare-eligible individuals and communities that may face barriers to healthcare access

  • Willingness and ability to travel occasionally within the assigned market

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supervising or collaborating with Advanced Practice Providers

  • Experience in value-based care, population health, or community-based healthcare

  • Medicare or Medicare Advantage experience

  • Home-based primary care or community-medicine experience

  • Experience supporting patients with complex medical, behavioral-health, or social needs

  • Population-health and quality-improvement experience

  • ACO, FQHC, managed-care, or other risk-based healthcare experience

  • Multi-site or market-level physician leadership experience

  • Experience leading clinical teams in a remote or geographically distributed environment

  • Passion for mentoring providers and building collaborative, high-performing care teams

What Success Looks Like

  • Providing trusted and responsive physician leadership across the Massachusetts market

  • Developing and supporting high-performing Nurse Practitioners and interdisciplinary care teams

  • Improving clinical quality, patient outcomes, and care coordination

  • Supporting value-based care goals and reducing avoidable hospitalizations

  • Building strong partnerships across clinical, operational, payer, and community stakeholders

  • Creating consistency in clinical workflows and standards of care

  • Driving continuous improvement throughout the assigned market

  • Supporting a positive, relationship-based experience for patients and team members

  • Serving as a physician leader who champions Matter Health’s mission, values, and commitment to leading with LOVE

Why Matter Health

We believe healthcare should be personal, proactive, and delivered in a way that meets patients where they are.

Every physician leader at Matter Health plays an essential role in improving healthcare access for individuals living in underserved communities while helping redefine how relationship-based primary care is delivered.

This is more than a leadership position. It is an opportunity to influence clinical strategy, develop providers, improve health outcomes, and help shape the future of community-based, value-driven healthcare.

Total Healthcare. Where you live.

Working at Matter Health

We believe in supporting the whole person—both professionally and personally. Benefits for full-time employees begin the first day of the month following the employee’s start date.

Health & Wellness

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Employer-funded HSA options

  • Employer-paid life and disability insurance

  • Voluntary supplemental insurance options

  • Access to Matter Health’s in-person and virtual care services

Financial Security

  • Competitive compensation

  • 401(k) with company match beginning on Day 60

  • Financial wellness resources

Time Away

  • Up to four weeks of Paid Time Off

  • 10 paid company holidays

  • Two paid Volunteer Days each year

Professional Growth

  • Annual CME allowance for continuing medical education and certifications

  • Dedicated paid CME days for conferences and professional development

  • Opportunity to help shape an innovative, value-based primary care model

  • Collaborative physician leadership team focused on mentorship and continuous improvement

  • Meaningful opportunities to influence clinical strategy, quality initiatives, and organizational growth

Eligibility is based on full-time employment status. Additional benefit details will be shared during the interview process.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Matter Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where every team member feels valued, respected, and empowered to make a difference.

Compensation Range: $254K - $312K

Part-Time HVAC Career Coach

(Flexible, Paid Workshops + Upside)

About CourseCareers

CourseCareers is an online education platform that helps people launch new careers without a college degree or prior experience.

We work with industry professionals to create job-focused courses that teach practical, employer-aligned skills in technology, business, and the skilled trades. Our students are career changers looking for realistic, entry-level opportunities — and coaching helps bridge the gap between coursework and landing the job.

About the Role

We’re looking for a part-time HVAC Career Coach to support students through live workshops and optional 1:1 coaching.

This is not a traditional employment role and not a guaranteed-income position. It’s a flexible, paid opportunity best suited for experienced HVAC technicians who enjoy mentoring, teaching, and helping others break into the trade — with upside if students choose to work with you.

How This Role Actually Works

  • You host a live, one-hour workshop (seminar-style) for students

  • You are paid $50 per workshop, plus any private coaching business you acquire

  • You may receive exclusive coaching opportunities based on performance and engagement

  • Workshops are used to provide value, answer questions, and showcase your real-world experience

  • If students choose to book you for 1:1 coaching, you keep the coaching revenue

  • You set your own availability and working hours

There is no requirement to convert students — workshops are paid regardless — but conversion is where the upside comes from.

Responsibilities

  • Host a live, one-hour workshop on a monthly basis

  • Answer student questions about HVAC careers and the job search

  • Share real-world insight into what entry-level HVAC roles, apprenticeships, and certifications actually look like

  • Provide optional 1:1 coaching to students who request it

What We’re Looking For

  • 3+ years of professional HVAC experience (residential, commercial, or industrial)

  • Familiarity with entry-level roles, apprenticeships, and certification pathways (EPA 608, etc.)

  • Interest in mentoring and helping career changers enter the trades

  • Strong communication and teaching ability

  • Availability at least three evenings per week, ideally Tuesday–Thursday

  • Self-starter mindset — comfortable leading workshops independently

Ideal Fit

This role is a great fit if you:

  • Enjoy teaching and mentoring

  • Want flexible, side income

  • Like the idea of being paid to teach — with optional upside

  • Don’t need guaranteed hours or full-time income

Compensation

  • $50 per one-hour workshop (One per month guaranteed)

  • Unlimited upside from 1:1 coaching sessions you convert

  • No caps, no quotas, no minimums

raw.description:
Lifecycle Marketing Manager

Remote (minimum 4-hour overlap with US Eastern hours) | Marketing | Reports to: Director, Revenue Marketing

Time Doctor is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own the marketing-led customer journey from the moment an account starts paying. You will decide who hears what, when, based on which behaviour, and toward which commercial outcome. Your job is to turn customer behaviour and usage signals into adoption, retention, expansion and reactivation revenue, and to run that engine AI-first, building agents and agentic workflows that do real work.

Who we are

Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.

The role

You will own the lifecycle marketing program for our paying customers: the 30/60/90 onboarding plays, ongoing customer communications, customer segmentation, and the expansion and retention plays that grow and keep the base. You design the journeys, brief the work, QA it and measure it, and you own the revenue outcome.

Three things define this seat.

  • The number. Your primary measure is the qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities Lifecycle generates and surfaces. Expansion revenue, net revenue retention and at-risk recovery sit right behind it, shared with CS, Sales and Product.

  • The lane. You own orchestration and outcomes across the customer base, not every surface you touch. PMM owns the message, GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and Growth and CS co-define the signals with you. You make it all work together.

  • The operating model. This is an AI-first role, and AI fluency is the job. The bar is that you can stand up an agent that does real work, not describe one. Accelerating Time Doctor's AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation of the seat.

This is a systems role. You build repeatable, automated journeys rather than one-off campaigns, and you keep human ownership of segmentation logic, offer design, guardrails, final QA and the commercial call.

Who you are

  • You treat a revenue number as yours, and you design every journey toward adoption, retention or expansion.

  • You have high agency. When a journey underperforms, you find out why and fix it.

  • You are commercially minded. You turn customer signals into revenue.

  • You are analytical and cohort-fluent. You read behaviour and act on where customers stall or grow.

  • You think in systems. You would rather build a repeatable, automated flow than run another one-off campaign.

  • You work cleanly across Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops without needing to own their surfaces, and you turn ambiguous boundaries into working agreements.

  • You build with AI. Agents and agentic workflows are how you get work done.

What you will own

  • Onboarding and adoption. The marketing-led 30/60/90 program that gets new paying customers to first value, plus ongoing adoption of key capabilities and education, including driving traffic to TD Academy and running education webinars end to end. You own the day-0 handoff: the trigger and the data that enrol a new customer in the right journey.

  • Segmentation and journey orchestration. Segmenting paying customers on profile, product usage, engagement, lifecycle stage, adoption state, expansion propensity and churn risk, then designing, building and QA-ing the journeys and triggers on top, so the right cohort gets the right play at the right moment.

  • Expansion and cross-sell. Plays that grow existing accounts through seats, add-ons and cross-sell. You co-define expansion signals with Growth and CS, turn them into segments and plays, and route qualified opportunities to Sales and CS, with GTM Ops implementing detection and actions.

  • Retention and win-back. Proactive plays against at-risk cohorts, air cover for CS retention efforts, re-engagement of dormant accounts, and win-back of churned accounts where it is commercially worthwhile.

  • Renewal-moment marketing. Value-recap and air-cover campaigns timed to the renewal window, reinforcing realised value ahead of the CS conversation.

  • Customer communications. Audience, segmentation, timing and orchestration for the customer newsletter, customer webinars, feature and release comms, and lifecycle-triggered in-app announcements. PMM owns the message. You own distribution.

  • Advocacy and review sites. Identifying advocates and triggering review, referral, testimonial and reference asks at the right lifecycle moment, including activating the promoters CS surfaces through NPS. You fully own review-site management and take the case studies Content and PMM produce to market.

  • Lifecycle analytics and experimentation. Performance across every journey, from onboarding completion and time-to-value through to expansion, retention, renewal support and win-back. You find where customers stall, drop off, expand or disengage, and you keep improving the programs.

  • AI in the workflow. Agentic workflows for segmentation, usage and account signal interpretation, journey and trigger build and testing, customer comms drafting and variants, propensity and churn scoring drafts, cohort analysis and drop-off detection. You decide what runs autonomously, what needs human judgement, and how each workflow gets operationalised with GTM Ops.

This role may not suit you if

  • You measure yourself on sends, opens and campaign volume rather than on revenue adopted, kept and grown.

  • You prefer launching one-off campaigns to building journeys that run on their own.

  • AI for you means prompt libraries and screenshots. We need someone who has built agents that do real work.

  • Your experience is mostly top-of-funnel. This role starts the moment an account becomes a paying customer.

  • You need to own every surface you touch. PMM owns the message and GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and this seat depends on working well with both.

  • You cannot commit to at least four hours a day of overlap with US Eastern business hours.

What a realistic week looks like

A cohort review showing where last month's new customers stalled before day 30, and a fix to the onboarding journey that ships the same week. A working session with CS on an at-risk cohort and the play you will run against it. Two expansion opportunities your signals surfaced, qualified and routed to Sales. An agent you built to draft and QA journey variants, tightened after its first run. A value-recap campaign going out to accounts entering their renewal window. Live collaboration during US Eastern hours, async for the rest of the day.

Requirements

Your experience

  • 5 to 7 years in lifecycle, CRM, customer or retention marketing at a B2B SaaS company.

  • A track record of designing and running behaviour-triggered customer journeys, with adoption, retention or expansion outcomes you owned. You know your numbers and can walk us through them.

  • Comfortable working from product-usage and account data to define segments, propensity and churn logic. You can specify the scoring and routing, even though GTM Ops builds it.

  • Fluent in a marketing automation or lifecycle stack such as HubSpot, and in cohort analysis.

  • Experience running expansion, cross-sell or renewal-support programs, and coordinating opportunity handoff with CS and Sales.

  • A clear understanding of where lifecycle ends and Growth and CS begin, and the ability to work cleanly across those lines.

  • Hands-on experience building agents or agentic workflows that do real work. You can show us what you built and what it does.

  • Remote, with a minimum four-hour daily overlap with US Eastern (ET) business hours.

Nice to have

  • Product-led SaaS experience.

  • More than four hours of daily overlap with US Eastern business hours.

  • Background in workforce analytics, time tracking, HR tech or productivity software.

  • Experience marketing to BPO, outsourcing, healthcare or tech services customers.

The team you are joining

You will report to our Director, Revenue Marketing. You will work closely with Growth and CS on expansion and churn signals, with PMM and Content on messaging and proof assets, with GTM Ops on scoring, routing and journey implementation, and with Sales and CS on the opportunities you hand forward.

How we will measure success

  • Qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities you generate and surface. This is the headline measure and the one you control most directly.

  • Expansion revenue, net revenue retention contribution and at-risk recovery, which CS, Sales and Product also influence.

  • Onboarding completion, time-to-value and product adoption depth among paying customers, as the leading indicators.

  • Advocacy volume across reviews, referrals and references, renewal-support coverage, and revenue recovered through win-back.

Your first 90 days

  • Days 1 to 30. Map the post-conversion journey and where customers stall. Audit the current 30/60/90 onboarding and customer comms. Document the conversion handoff: the trigger and the data that must travel with a new customer. Agree the first expansion and churn signals with Growth and CS, and baseline adoption, retention and expansion.

  • Days 31 to 60. Launch or repair the 30/60/90 onboarding. Stand up the first expansion play and one renewal-moment campaign. Set up cohort reporting, introduce AI-assisted segmentation and comms, and get review-site management and one advocacy trigger (NPS promoters from CS) live.

  • Days 61 to 90. Scale the expansion and retention plays that are working. Run a win-back pilot. Establish expansion-opportunity routing to Sales and CS with GTM Ops, then present the adoption, retention and expansion baseline alongside a lifecycle roadmap.

Why this role

  • You own a real revenue number, from the moment a customer converts.

  • You get a clear lane. Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops are your partners, and your focus is orchestration and outcomes.

  • You work AI-first from day one, at a company where accelerating an AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation.

  • We are profitable and bootstrapped. Your budget comes from customers, not from a burn rate.

  • Fully remote and flexible, working with talented people in 30+ countries.

Our hiring approach

Because this is an AI-first role, our process asks you to prove it. Expect a working session where you show agents or agentic workflows you have built, then stand up or walk through one live, applied to a real customer-lifecycle problem. Prompt libraries and screenshots are not enough. We want to see how you architect, orchestrate and operationalise the work.

This is a full-time, 100% remote role. We are an equal opportunity employer and we value diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.

We hire globally, and this particular role requires a minimum four-hour daily overlap with US Eastern business hours. Our Talent Attraction team will walk you through the details during your first conversation.

Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

Silvus Technologies is dedicated to one mission: connecting those who keep us safe. We do so by delivering the most advanced Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET) radios powered by our custom and ever evolving Mobile-Networked MIMO waveform. Together, our radios and waveform provide vital communications for mission-critical applications in the harshest environments from underground tunnels to high-altitude balloons.
Silvus StreamCaster™ radios are being rapidly adopted by customers all over the world ranging from the U.S. and Allied Nations Departments of Defense to International, Federal, State, and Local Law Enforcement agencies, all the way to the Superbowl, Grammys, and industry-leading drone, robot, and unmanned systems manufacturers.

Would you like to join an incredibly talented group of people, doing very challenging work, with the prime directive of “Keeping Our Heroes Connected”?

Silvus’ rapid growth is fueled by a focus on research and innovation and a team of the most passionate, skilled, and creative thinking individuals. If you are looking for a challenging experience, you owe it to yourself to learn how Silvus can be the next chapter of your career.


Job Description


THE OPPORTUNITY

Silvus Technologies is seeking an International Sales Engineer to collaborate closely with the Sales, Marketing, and Business Development teams, providing our customers with tailored solutions that meet their needs.

The successful individual in this role will participate in technical sales, demonstrations, and support of Silvus' family of advanced multi-antenna MIMO radio and mesh networking solutions. Sales Engineers also play a key role in influencing product development. This opportunity is well suited for an entrepreneurial technologist who enjoys interacting with customers, has a healthy sense of adventure, and enjoys traveling.

This position is 100% remote.

Candidates must be based in Ukraine to be eligible for remote work and travel across the country.


The following is a list of at least some of the current essential job functions of the position. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities at any time at its discretion.


ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:


  • Provide pre- and post-sales technical support, including system planning, customer training, system optimization, etc.

  • Collect and analyze field failures and abnormalities; provide feedback to the development team.
  • Participate in resource allocation and hardware maintenance to support different sales and business development activities.
  • Help design engineers reproduce and troubleshoot problems; help drive future product development.
  • Perform other related duties of which the above are representative.
  • Travel up to 50% of the time for frequent travel for meetings, events, and demonstrations.

  • Proven hands-on experience in building, configuring, or operating drones using digital data links, with direct experience utilizingSilvus Technologies systems strongly preferred
  • Proficiency with radio frequency instruments such as signal generators and spectrum analyzers
  • Fluent Ukrainian and proficiency in English are required
  • Must be based in Ukraine
  • Eligibility to obtain relevant security clearances is required
  • Willingness to travel to potential conflict areas in support of radios

All employment is contingent upon the successful clearance of a background check.


PREFERRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:


  • Experience with operating and testing IP radios/modems.

raw.description:
Back-Office Insurance & Prior Authorization

Remote | Behavioral Health | 30 hours/week | $5-$6/hour
Working Hours: 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM US Central Time

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Back-Office Insurance & Prior Authorization Virtual Medical Assistant to support a nonprofit behavioral health organization in the United States.

This position will focus primarily on the administrative and insurance-related work required to move patients successfully through enrollment and prepare them for care.

The clinic serves patients using multiple payer arrangements, including commercial insurance, Medicaid, self-pay, and nonprofit programs that may reduce or eliminate the patient's cost of care. Because each patient may require a different process, the successful candidate must be highly organized and capable of determining what documentation, eligibility verification, authorization, or follow-up is needed for each case.

You will also help address existing administrative backlogs and build reliable back-office processes that the organization can continue using as it grows.

Key Responsibilities

Insurance Verification & Benefits

  • Verify patient eligibility and applicable benefits with commercial insurance plans and Medicaid.

  • Review payer information and document verification results accurately in AdvancedMD and related clinic systems.

  • Identify insurance requirements, coverage issues, or missing information that could prevent a patient from progressing through enrollment.

Prior Authorizations

  • Initiate and process prior authorization requests according to payer and clinic requirements.

  • Communicate with insurance representatives and use payer portals to obtain requirements, authorization status, and supporting information.

  • Track pending authorization requests and follow them through approval, denial, or other appropriate resolution.

Financial Eligibility & Patient Follow-Up

  • Review patient information and required documentation to determine potential eligibility for nonprofit financial assistance or reduced-cost programs.

  • Conduct outbound follow-up with patients regarding missing forms, insurance information, signatures, or other incomplete enrollment or eligibility requirements.

  • Maintain accurate documentation of eligibility status and pending requirements, and coordinate with the front-desk VMA once the patient is ready to proceed toward scheduling.

Patient Intake & Enrollment

  • Support patient intake by setting up patient profiles and portals, collecting required forms, and ensuring demographic and insurance information is complete and accurately documented.

  • Review intake documentation for missing or incomplete information and conduct outbound follow-up with patients to obtain required forms, signatures, insurance details, or other enrollment requirements.

  • Track each patient through the intake and enrollment process, coordinate with the front-desk VMA, and confirm that all required administrative steps are completed before the patient proceeds to scheduling.

Provider Credentialing Support

  • Assist with provider insurance credentialing and payer enrollment as the clinic expands the scope of the position.

  • Organize required credentialing documents, payer correspondence, application statuses, and renewal information.

  • Follow up on pending credentialing items and communicate outstanding requirements to the appropriate clinic team member.

EHR & Chart Preparation

  • Update patient demographics, insurance information, authorization details, financial eligibility information, and related administrative records in AdvancedMD.

  • Prepare patient charts before appointments and confirm that required administrative documents are complete and available.

  • Identify incomplete or inconsistent information and resolve or escalate issues before the patient's scheduled visit.

Backlog & Case Management

  • Review outstanding patient and administrative cases and prioritize them based on urgency, status, and required next action.

  • Determine what is preventing each case from progressing and take appropriate follow-up action with the patient, payer, or internal team.

  • Maintain clear documentation of outreach attempts, completed work, pending items, and next steps until each case reaches resolution.

Cross-Functional Administrative Support

  • Provide additional healthcare administrative support during available capacity and as cross-training develops.

  • Coordinate closely with the bilingual front-desk VMA to ensure patients transition smoothly between inquiry, enrollment, insurance processing, and scheduling.

  • Provide coverage for related workflows when appropriately trained and within the defined scope of the position.

SOP & Process Development

  • Help document insurance verification, prior authorization, financial eligibility, and enrollment follow-up procedures.

  • Update Standard Operating Procedures as payer requirements and clinic workflows are clarified or improved.

  • Identify recurring back-office bottlenecks and recommend processes that improve consistency, accuracy, and turnaround time.

Required Qualifications

  • Previous healthcare experience with substantial responsibility for insurance verification and prior authorizations.

  • Experience working with US commercial insurance plans, Medicaid, or both.

  • Experience contacting insurance companies and using payer portals.

  • Strong understanding of healthcare eligibility and authorization workflows.

  • Experience using an EHR or practice-management system.

  • Strong administrative documentation and data-entry skills.

  • High attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Strong follow-up, organization, and task-management skills.

  • Professional verbal and written English communication.

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple pending cases.

  • Strong understanding of HIPAA and patient confidentiality requirements.

  • Reliable attendance and punctuality.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Behavioral health or mental health administrative experience.

  • Experience with AdvancedMD.

  • Experience evaluating patient financial eligibility.

  • Experience supporting Medicaid populations.

  • Provider credentialing or payer enrollment experience.

  • English and Spanish bilingual proficiency.

Systems & Tools

The clinic uses or expects the VMA to work with:

  • AdvancedMD

  • Microsoft Teams

  • Phone services

  • Insurance payer portals

  • Patient intake portals and online forms

  • VPN and secure remote-access systems

  • Time Doctor

Remote Work Requirements

Candidates must maintain:

  • Private and secure home workspace

  • Reliable computer capable of supporting healthcare applications and multiple browser-based systems

  • Stable primary internet connection, reliable backup internet

  • Verified backup power source

  • Professional headset

  • Secondary monitor

  • Quiet working environment appropriate for patient and insurance calls

What Success Looks Like

Success in this position requires strong ownership and follow-through.

The ideal candidate does not simply complete individual insurance tasks. You should be able to look at a pending patient case, determine what is preventing it from moving forward, identify the next action, complete the necessary follow-up, and continue managing the case until the appropriate resolution has been reached.

You will help ensure patients do not remain unnecessarily stuck in the enrollment process because of missing documentation, incomplete insurance requirements, pending authorizations, or administrative backlogs.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for product managers to own product areas within Doit's AI Neobank App.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.

What You'll Own

  • Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.

  • Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.

  • Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.

  • Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.

  • Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

  • Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

  • Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

  • Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

  • Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

  • Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

  • Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

  • High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

  • Can make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.

  • Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.

  • Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only write decks and do not drive execution.

  • PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.

  • Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.

  • People who launch features and then stop caring.

  • PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Australia. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Australia.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

raw.excerpt: Assistant Professors are full-time employed faculty who provide a variety of educational services to degree, certificate, and non-degree learners.
raw.description:
Assistant Professors are full-time employed faculty who provide a variety of educational services to degree, certificate, and non-degree learners. Assistant Professors are responsible for meeting the expectations and requirements of Capella University while establishing and maintaining effective relationships with learners, colleagues, staff, and administration. Assistant Professors are able to perform well in all key accountabilities of the role, are nimble and flexible and expected to be able and willing to take on essential roles and other duties as needed, within the department, school or university. Assistant Professors ensure that learners receive quality educational experiences consistent with stated course outcomes as well as HLC and any program accreditation standards. They provide high-quality, impactful, and inclusive experiences that deliver exceptional learning outcomes. Capella values the scholarly-practitioner model and expects Assistant Professors to continue learning and development through participation in scholarly activities or professional practice in the discipline. Among the responsibilities that Assistant Professors are expected to perform include: teaching (online), mentor and committee work (graduate level only), and contributing to curriculum development. Assistant Professors also participate in school governance through faculty committees and may participate in a variety of other activities based upon the university’s needs and the faculty member’s unique skill set.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Teaching and Instruction – Assistant Professors are highly engaged instructors in the courses and residencies they teach. They are sought out by learners and consistently exceed set expectations for faculty who teach courses at Capella. Assistant Professors use course data to constantly improve their individual teaching performance and contribute regularly to the improvement and refinement of the courses they teach. Regularly reviews course feedback and implements change to continually strengthen performance and enhance learner experience.

  • Doctoral Mentoring – Assistant Professors are highly knowledgeable about established dissertation and doctoral capstone processes and resources. They interact effectively with learners, develop strong relationships and offer guidance. They have demonstrated success in chairing and serving on doctoral committees. Assistant Professors facilitate highly interactive dissertation and capstone course-rooms and their learners are supported to timely completion of the dissertation or capstone product.

  • Curriculum and Course Development – Assistant Professors are knowledgeable in the Capella course development process and have demonstrated the ability to work successfully with cross functional partners across Capella to plan and deliver high quality course and curriculum in the area of their expertise. Participates in the design development and continuous improvement of courses and course materials including course plans, objectives, and outcomes, teaching aids, competency-based assessments, and authentic assessment tools. Ensures sensitivity diversity and inclusiveness in curriculum design, course content, and study materials as needed.

  • School and University Governance – Assistant Professors regularly demonstrate leadership roles in school and university governance. They willingly assume school and university committee roles as active participants and are effective in driving the positive impact of these governance structures. They are the role models and leaders among faculty and serve as peer mentors.

  • Professional Service and Practice – Assistant Professors are active in contributing their professional knowledge and skills to the needs of their local communities and within their professional network affiliations. They carry the “Capella Brand” and mission to their local regions and communities. Research and Scholarship – Assistant Professors stay current in their scholarly field(s) and demonstrate expertise through writing, speaking and conference attendance.

  • Leadership through Team Engagement – Assistant Professors are expected to take on essential roles and other duties as needed, within the department, school or university. Bringing their unique skills and perspectives, Assistant Professors regularly contribute to departmental leadership whether it be through specific roles, active contribution of innovative ideas, or taking on challenging tasks. All full-time faculty are depended on, and relied upon, for immediate and unplanned needs and must be nimble and adjust to changes as they occur. These roles may include specialized assignments such as faculty and cross functional staff meetings, commencement, residencies, Capella-sponsored faculty development, problem resolution, faculty orientation/mentoring, webinar facilitation, course revisions, etc.

  • Additionally, some Assistant Professors may have certain “areas of emphasis” where a greater degree of leadership is expected and include such as specialized responsibilities or coordinating functions in support of the school’s educational goals such as Learner Management, Research and Advising, Program Development and Advising, Field Education, Accreditation or support of B2B partnership efforts. Responsibility areas and specific assignments are based on the needs of the school and capabilities of the faculty member. Faculty assignments and areas of emphasis may vary significantly from school to school; however, the position is structured to ensure the faculty member is able to contribute optimally to essential teaching and related support services to learners.

Job Skills:

Teaching and Assessment and/or Doctoral Mentoring:

Refers to the ability to enable learner academic progression, provide guidance, and enhance learner experience.

  • Understand and apply Capella’s competency-based education model that aligns program outcomes, competencies, assessments, and reports with external standards and Capella educational philosophy to improve learning.

  • Convey and share content knowledge and relevant professional experience in the discipline.

  • Facilitate learner acquisition of course and/or research competencies aligned with their program.

  • Consider learner differences and appreciate the diversity of experience and interpretation among learners.

  • Effectively assess and document learner knowledge, skills, and dispositions through formative and summative feedback. Monitor learner progress and achievement, and refers learners to additional resources as needed.

  • Display cultural awareness and sensitivity to learner differences and seek information about strengths, needs, and interests of the learner to provide personalized support.

  • Engage learners in effective, timely, and relevant interactions and nurtures a learning community that cultivates a spirit of trust, interaction, and learning.

  • Effectively manage key online course and/or advanced doctoral processes and tools.

  • Provide a timely, visible, consistent, and responsive presence in the courseroom and/or mentoring process, and communicate appropriately and respectfully.

  • Encourage learner engagement consistent with the learner code of conduct and support the free exchange of ideas.

Research and Scholarship:

These activities advance teaching and mentoring as well as professional development. Activity varies by person and field. Meeting research and scholarship requirements as defined by external accreditors, where appropriate. Schools may identify focus areas of research, specific conferences, or professional journals.

  • Scholarship for applying innovative teaching methods, especially those that can be empirically validated as having a positive impact on learner success (e.g., course success, continuation, graduation).

  • Submit proposals and/or present at workshops or conferences (internally and externally).

  • Showcase original/innovative work/exhibition.

  • Maintain an active research agenda.

  • Attend professional development events, attain continuing education credits, and pursue additional credentials.

  • Present research (whether applied or teaching-focused).

  • Submit paper and/or publish at industry-recognized channels.

Professional Service and Practice:

Includes external-facing activities related to learners, institution, profession, and/or community. Activities increase the service of the institution and strengthen its external reputation. Meeting professional service and practice requirements as defined by external accreditors, where appropriate. In most situations, the acitivities are with reduced-fee/pro bono/honorarium.

  • To learners: Career and well-being advising, leading student organizations, guidance on learning and projects outside of courseroom, learner-facing webinars.

  • To institution: Providing support for institutional activities with external audience (e.g., presentations for employer partners, job fairs, representing the institution at conferences).

  • To profession: Leadership in organizations or professional associations, advocacy for the advancement of the profession and communities served, organize professional conferences.

  • To community: Sharing knowledge with the public, volunteer for community-based events with their expertise (e.g., volunteering at clinics for underprivileged communities).

Governance and Leadership:

Include internal-facing activities to increase the effectiveness of the institution, the school, and faculty practice.

  • Active participation in appropriate program, department, school, or university committees, providing expertise and perspectives to advance university and school’s strategic direction.

  • Active participation in faculty staff meetings, Capella-sponsored faculty development, and other faculty-focused events (e.g. CU Faculty Virtual Conference), including sharing best practices, providing personal expertise via different communication channels, promoting better community support among peers, etc.

  • Serve as SMEs in course and program development; support for accreditation efforts; and serve in pilot groups for innovation projects at program, school, or university levels.

  • Identify and orchestrate the proactive management of curriculum content quality and currency. Demonstrate expertise in evaluating and coordinating the ongoing assessment of content to ensure its relevance, accuracy, and up-to-date nature.

  • Take on additional, challenging projects to serve the needs of the school or university in support of learner success.

  • Provide mentorship, feedback, and guidance to other faculty members when appropriate.

Performance Criteria:

  • Satisfactory performance of teaching and/or mentoring activities based on the university faculty expectations is required and will be reviewed as part of the annual plan of work and review process.

Work Experience:

  • Three or more years teaching in an online setting highly preferred.

  • Experience teaching in higher education required.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for Android engineers to build the native Android experience for Doit's AI Neobank App.

This role is for someone who cares about clean user flows, fast performance, product quality and shipping reliable mobile features used by real customers.

What You'll Own

  • Build and ship Android features using Kotlin.

  • Create clean mobile flows for insurance, payments, claims, renewals and financial services.

  • Work with product and design to simplify complex user journeys.

  • Integrate backend APIs and ensure mobile flows are stable, secure and reliable.

  • Improve app performance, crash rate, loading states, responsiveness and memory usage.

  • Use analytics, user behaviour and production issues to improve the product.

  • Build AI-assisted mobile experiences only where they genuinely improve the user journey.

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

  • Strong Android fundamentals and experience shipping production apps.

  • Good knowledge of Jetpack, Coroutines, Flow and modern Android architecture.

  • Strong sense of mobile UX, usability, edge cases and user flows.

  • Experience integrating REST APIs and debugging production issues.

  • Fast execution, high ownership and strong attention to product quality.

  • App links, GitHub, screenshots or examples of shipped work are a strong advantage.

Tech Stack

  • Kotlin

  • Jetpack Compose

  • Android SDK

  • Coroutines & Flow

  • SQL / NoSQL

  • TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Thinks in user journeys, not just screens.

  • Cares about making complex financial products feel simple.

  • Moves fast without creating messy code.

  • Notices UX, performance and reliability issues before users complain.

  • Honest about what they personally built, what was team-owned and what impact they can or cannot claim.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who only want fully defined tickets.

  • Developers who build screens without caring about user experience.

  • People who ignore crashes, edge cases, loading states or performance.

  • Engineers who move slowly in a startup environment.

  • People who exaggerate impact without explaining their actual contribution.

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Philippines. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Philippines.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

At GoalPoint Behavior Group, we are passionate about transforming lives through compassionate, evidence-based care. Founded on the principles of integrity, innovation, and inclusion, we provide high-quality Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) services to children and families across Georgia. Our mission is to help each child reach their full potential by delivering personalized, family-centered treatment that is rooted in clinical excellence and supported by a collaborative team approach.

We are a team of dedicated professionals—Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs), Registered Behavior Technicians (RBTs), and support staff—committed to creating meaningful change in the lives of the individuals we serve. We value continuous learning, teamwork, and a positive work environment where every team member is respected, empowered, and given the tools to succeed.

If you’re driven by purpose, committed to quality, and want to make a lasting impact, GoalPoint is the place for you.

Remote Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) – Georgia Licensed

Based out of Warner Robins, GA | 1099 Contract | Part-Time or Full-Time | Pediatrics & Early Intervention

Overview

We are seeking a Georgia-licensed Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our clinical team based out of our Warner Robins, Georgia location, while providing services remotely via telehealth. This is a 1099 contract position with flexibility for part-time or full-time availability.

In this role, you will focus on pediatric and early intervention services, providing clinical oversight, assessments, treatment planning, and collaboration—while being supported by Speech-Language Pathology Assistants (SLPAs) who assist with service delivery under your supervision. This structure allows you to focus on high-level clinical decision-making while maintaining a manageable and efficient caseload.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct remote evaluations and assessments for pediatric clients
  • Diagnose speech, language, voice, and/or swallowing disorders using evidence-based practices
  • Develop, update, and oversee individualized treatment plans
  • Provide direct teletherapy services as clinically indicated
  • Supervise and collaborate with SLPAs, including review of session notes, progress, and treatment implementation
  • Offer clinical guidance and feedback to SLPA staff to ensure quality and compliance
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary team members to support coordinated care
  • Educate caregivers and families on communication strategies and home carryover
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation in compliance with Georgia licensure and payer requirements
  • Participate in team meetings, care coordination, and clinical consultation as needed

Qualifications & Experience

  • Active Georgia SLP license (required)
  • Master’s degree in Speech-Language Pathology from an accredited program
  • Experience working with pediatric populations, especially early intervention, strongly preferred
  • Prior school-based or pediatric clinical experience highly desirable
  • Experience supervising or working alongside SLPAs preferred (training/support provided if needed)
  • Strong knowledge of speech and swallowing anatomy, physiology, and development
  • Comfortable providing services via telehealth platforms
  • Excellent communication skills with families, assistants, and multidisciplinary teams
  • Organized, self-directed, and able to manage a remote caseload effectively

Position Details

  • Work Type: 1099 Independent Contractor
  • Schedule: Flexible – Part-Time or Full-Time
  • Location: Remote (clinically based out of Warner Robins, GA)
  • Caseload: Pediatrics & Early Intervention
  • Support: SLPA support provided
  • Hours: Flexible with opportunity to increase based on availability and interest

Why Join Us

  • Fully remote clinical work with a local clinical home base
  • SLPA support to streamline service delivery
  • Flexible scheduling and autonomy
  • Collaborative, clinically driven team environment
  • Opportunity for additional hours and expanded responsibilities

Job Types: Full-time, Contract

Work Location: Remote
